text:
Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle in quantum mechanics can be compared to trying to take a high-resolution photograph of a speeding car. If you use a very fast shutter speed to freeze the car's exact position in the frame, the image becomes sharp, but you lose all sense of how fast it was moving because there's no motion blur. Conversely, if you use a slower shutter speed to capture the blur and convey the car's speed (momentum), the car's precise location within that blur becomes indistinct. This illustrates that in the quantum world, you cannot simultaneously know both the exact position and the exact momentum of a particle with perfect precision.

The name of the planet humans live on is Earth.
